narration: This plane has no wings, and it was just dropped from a B-52.
It is NASA's M2-F2, over California in nineteen sixty six.
Its body shape makes the lift. The same idea later helped shape the space shuttle.
On its first flight, it fell away at forty five thousand feet.
outcome: The M2-F2 glided all the way down and landed on the dry lakebed at Edwards.
title: Wingless plane dropped from a B-52
description:
In 1966, NASA's M2-F2 lifting body, a research aircraft with no wings, was drop-launched from a B-52 mothership over California and glided back to a landing on the dry lakebed at Edwards Air Force Base.

extra_sources.excerpt: The M2-F2 and the other lifting-body designs were all attached to a wing pylon on NASA’s B-52 mothership and carried aloft. The vehicles were then drop-launched and, at the end of their flights, glided back to wheeled landings on the dry lake or runway at Edwards AFB. The lifting body designs influenced the design of the Space Shuttle and were also reincarnated in the design of the X-38 in the 1990s.

Milt Thompson was the pilot. By then, the same B-52 used to air launch the famed X-15 rocket research aircraft was modified to also carry the lifting bodies. Thompson was dropped from the B-52's wing pylon mount at an altitude of 45,000 feet on that maiden glide flight.
